newsitem.title: USA: MGE spring wheat ends lower on hedge selling.
newsitem.headline: MGE spring wheat ends lower on hedge selling.

text.p: MGE spring wheat futures succumbed to hedge selling and settled lower in a heavily traded session, traders said.
"We were ahead at the midsesion on...enormous commercial buying. But Chicago wheat and beans started breaking, and enough hedge selling came in to push us down," an MGE trader said.

U.S. wheat markets remained under pressure from active harvesting and reports of better-than-expected yields. Favorable weekend weather should allow harvest to progress rapidly in the southern Kansas and in Oklahoma and Texas.
A featured element of Friday's trade was speculative short money being rolled into deferred contracts, traders said.
MGE spring wheat settled 2-3/4 to 5-1/4 cents lower, with July down 3-1/2 cents at $3.80-1/4 per bushel. New-crop September slipped 2-3/4 cents to close at $3.67-1/4.
Dealings were brisk during Friday's session, and the MGE estimated spring wheat futures volume at 35.38 million bushels.
